A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same O3-D research work. Their complete main text and supplementary material, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 12 VLMs and DepthAnything V2 on O3-D, including depth-ordering accuracy, cue sensitivity and language-bias analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and the supplementary experiments.

M1.justification: The scene-generation and cue-control procedures, depth-ordering task, prompting approach and SDGM methodology are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic and real O3-D coverage, including zero-cue, single-cue, two-cue and mixed-cue images. Dataset counts and task requirements are unchanged.

E2.justification: The same 12 VLMs and DepthAnything V2 baseline participate in the same comparisons. DepthAnything V2's citation changes from reference 57 to 56 without changing the comparator.

E3.justification: Image preprocessing, model configurations, prompt sampling, response parsing, metrics and ICL/CoT demonstration settings are identical, including the supplementary settings.

E4.justification: The cue-strength and cue-interaction analyses, near-far bias tests, ICL/CoT comparisons, referring-clarity analyses and supplementary cue correlations are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is unchanged, including the 95% confidence intervals in supplementary Figure 4. No run counts, seed information or statistical estimation procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match across versions, including main Table 4 and supplementary Tables 1 and 6–11. The plotted results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The near-far bias definition, SDGM formula and modified-SDGM formulation and reasoning in supplementary Section 8 are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about O3-D, weak depth-cue utilization, stronger language influence and limited ICL/CoT benefits.

C2.justification: Interpretations of cue utilization, language sensitivity and near-far bias are unchanged. Qualifications concerning focus and linear-perspective cues, and future extensions to motion and binocular cues, are also retained.

D1.justification: Both versions provide the same code/data release link, rendering and preprocessing details, prompt examples, model-version table and SDGM implementation examples.

R1.justification: v1 references 53 and 54 duplicate Watt et al.'s 'Focus cues affect perceived depth'; v2 retains this work as reference 53. No distinct cited work or substantive research positioning is added or removed.

P1.justification: v2 removes the duplicate bibliography entry and updates affected citation numbers throughout the main text and supplement. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; prose and section structure otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Deleting the duplicate entry shifts subsequent references upward on PDF page 18. Figures and tables retain their design and placement; affected captions only receive updated citation numbers.

improvement.justification: Consolidating the duplicate Watt et al. reference tidies the bibliography but does not meaningfully alter overall quality. The scientific content, supporting evidence, explanations and reproducibility information remain unchanged throughout the main paper and supplement.
